summary: Repo-owned coordination layer for the full Steven Woods public suite. Per-project manifests remain the factual status layer; this file is the judgment layer for priority, quality, likely current work, and next-step tradeoffs.
use_this_page_for: Keep one durable portfolio-level mental model in the repo instead of in chat only.
Separate factual project status from portfolio judgment, so the manifest exports can stay factual while priority and time-energy-value tradeoffs can change faster.
Make reprioritization explicit by editing one small source file and rerendering the public and repo-readable overview surfaces.
update_workflow: Update the owning project manifest or archive manifest first when factual project status changes.
Edit this file when priority_now, likely_current_work, next_step, quality_note, or drift_note changes materially.
Rerun python3 tools/render_project_suite_overview.py after either kind of change.
Rerun python3 tools/render_index.py when the top-level public index should pick up reference-page changes.
tev_rules: Protect already-public software and reference surfaces before starting wide new research lanes.
Prefer publish-refresh work when local archive or documentation progress already exists but the public surface is behind; that is often the best time-energy-value move.
Use small seeding passes for scaffolded archives instead of broad redesigns.
Treat this overview as the place to reprioritize, and the per-project manifests as the place to state factual current status.

priority_bands.label: Protect public surfaces
priority_bands.description: Keep already-public software, docs, and dashboards trustworthy before expanding scope.

priority_bands.label: Publish local progress
priority_bands.description: High-value, usually lower-energy work where repo docs or manifests are already ahead of the public surface.

priority_bands.label: Steady advance
priority_bands.description: Important ongoing work that benefits from regular small batches rather than a one-off push.

priority_bands.label: Seed and clarify
priority_bands.description: Early-stage areas where a small baseline is more valuable than broad exploration.

priority_bands.label: Private tracking
priority_bands.description: Keep only a high-level public summary while the underlying work remains private.

aurora-galactica.likely_current_work: Post-release follow-through on the Aurora and Platinum public family, including lane trust, Galaxy Guardians readiness, and cleaner platform-versus-application seams.
aurora-galactica.next_step: Do a quick cross-branch status refresh before any shared-public publish so the Aurora manifest and the active release lane are not out of sync.
aurora-galactica.quality_note: This is the strongest product-style public surface in the suite, so small inconsistencies are disproportionately expensive.
aurora-galactica.drift_note: Live public main is ahead of this branch on Aurora. Treat Aurora as a cross-branch verification check whenever this repo branch is used for shared-public publishing.
aurora-galactica.coordination_note: Best handled as protect-and-verify work rather than broad redesign.

confidential-project.likely_current_work: Private rental-portal delivery and related product execution.
confidential-project.next_step: Keep the public summary minimal and accurate; do not expand the public surface unless there is a deliberate client-safe artifact to add.
confidential-project.quality_note: The public/private boundary is already clear, which is the main quality goal here.
confidential-project.coordination_note: Track only high-level continuity in public.

ai-dystopia-quotes.coordination_note: A good example of a healthy incremental export loop.

phd-renovation.coordination_note: Good candidate for steady, bounded progress rather than urgent intervention.
